'''Maureen L. Condic''' is an American neurobiology professor, bioethicist, ombudsman, and appointee to the United States's [[National Science Board]] currently at the [[Catholic University of America]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/crashing-boards-neuroscientist-maureen-condic-brings-different-voice-nsf-oversight-body|title=Crashing the boards: Neuroscientist Maureen Condic brings a different voice to NSF oversight body|date=2018-11-25|work=Science {{!}} AAAS|access-date=2018-12-01|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=http://www.kuer.org/post/utah-professor-tapped-oversee-national-science-foundation-widely-cited-anti-abortion-groups#stream/0|title=Utah Professor Tapped To Oversee National Science Foundation, Widely Cited By Anti-Abortion Groups|last=Neumann|first=Erik|access-date=2018-12-01|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.utahbusiness.com/university-of-utah-national-science-board/|title=White House Names University of Utah Bioethicist Maureen Condic to Six-Year Term on National Science Board - Utah Business|date=2018-11-08|work=Utah Business|access-date=2018-12-01|language=en-US|archive-date=2018-12-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181201093429/https://www.utahbusiness.com/university-of-utah-national-science-board/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=University |first=Catholic |title=Welcoming Dr. H. Joseph Yost as Senior Vice Provost for Research |url=https://president.catholic.edu/communication/welcoming-dr-h-joseph-yost-as-senior-vice-provost-for-research.html |access-date=2025-01-03 |website=The Catholic University of America |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
Condic received her BA from the [[University of Chicago]], and her PhD from the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. Her postdoctoral fellowship was undertaken at the [[University of Minnesota]]. She is an associate professor of neurobiology and anatomy at the [[University of Utah]] since 1997. Among her research contributions have been investigations into spinal cord development and regeneration,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=condic+ml+and+spinal&sort=date&size=20|title = Condic ml and spinal - Search Results - PubMed}}</ref> [[death]] determination,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Condic|first=Maureen L.|date=2016|title=Determination of Death: A Scientific Perspective on Biological Integration|url=https://philpapers.org/rec/CONDOD|journal=Journal of Medicine and Philosophy|volume=41|issue=3|pages=257–278|doi=10.1093/jmp/jhw004|pmid=27075193|pmc=4889815}}</ref> ethics around pregnancy,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Condic|first1=Maureen L.|last2=Harrison|first2=Donna|date=2018-06-18|title=Treatment of an Ectopic Pregnancy|journal=The Linacre Quarterly|language=en|volume=85|issue=3|pages=241–251|doi=10.1177/0024363918782417|issn=0024-3639|pmc=6161225|pmid=30275609}}</ref> [[Stem cell laws and policy in the United States|stem cell]] usage<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2009/04/16/does-research-really-need-human-embryos-and-cloning|title=Does Research Really Need Human Embryos and Cloning?|last=Condic|first=Dr Maureen L.|date=2009-04-16|work=The Daily Beast|access-date=2018-12-01|language=en}}</ref> and development.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Condic|first=Maureen L.|date=2014-04-15|title=Totipotency: What It Is and What It Is Not|journal=Stem Cells and Development|volume=23|issue=8|pages=796–812|doi=10.1089/scd.2013.0364|issn=1547-3287|pmc=3991987|pmid=24368070}}</ref> In a 2018 ''Science'' interview, Condic was asked why she moved from being well established in her field of neuroscience (with a 2001 single-author paper in her field's leading journal reporting that alterations in a single gene could help adult neurons regenerate,<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.jneurosci.org/content/21/13/4782.long | doi=10.1523/JNEUROSCI.21-13-04782.2001 | title=Adult Neuronal Regeneration Induced by Transgenic Integrin Expression | year=2001 | last1=Condic | first1=Maureen L. | journal=The Journal of Neuroscience | volume=21 | issue=13 | pages=4782–4788 | pmid=11425905 | pmc=6762359 }}</ref> and with two grants from the National Institutes of Health) into the then new field of bioethics. Condic said she moved due to a "heart-wrenching conversation" with a person suffering from a spinal cord injury concerning lack of availability of medical information, combined with concerns that the public was given false enthusiasm for spinal cord recovery after the injury to actor [[Christopher Reeve]].<ref name=":0" />

Since that transition, Condic has published extensively in the field of bioethics, including two books on the intricacies of fetal development and how this biological knowledge intersects with philosophical understandings of human beings, "Human Embryos, Human Beings: A Scientific and Philosophical Approach" (2018)<ref>{{Cite book|isbn=978-0813230238|title=Human Embryos, Human Beings: A Scientific and Philosophical Approach|last1=Condic|first1=Samuel B.|last2=Condic|first2=Maureen L.|date=29 June 2018|publisher=CUA Press }}</ref> and "Untangling Twinning: What Science Tells Us about the Nature of Human Embryos" (2020).<ref>{{Cite book|isbn=978-0268107055|title=Untangling Twinning: What Science Tells Us about the Nature of Human Embryos|last1=Condic|first1=Maureen L.|year=2020|publisher=University of Notre Dame Press }}</ref>

== Government service ==
Condic was appointed to the National Science Board to help advise the US Government's senior leaders on bioethics matters. Her term runs 2018–2024.<ref name=":2" /> She wrote an Affidavit in 2012 with expert testimony intended to inform the Oklahoma legislature on embryonic development and personhood.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://studylib.net/doc/6856685/appendix-a-affidavit-of-dr.-maureen-l.-condic--ph.d.-stat...|title=APPENDIX A Affidavit of Dr. Maureen L. Condic, Ph.D. STATE OF|work=studylib.net|access-date=2018-12-01|language=en}}</ref> In 2013, she testified before Congress regarding ethics surrounding a bill to ban abortions past a certain timeframe.<ref>{{Citation|last=Biblical Creation & Apologetics Ministries|title=Dr Maureen Condic Congressional Testimony: Fetal Pain at 8 Weeks...|date=2017-04-12|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0CTzJRF8v24|access-date=2018-12-01}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

On July 29, 2021, Condic submitted an amicus brief<ref>{{cite web |title=Dobbs Amicus Brief |url=https://lozierinstitute.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/CLI-Dobbs-Amicus-Brief.pdf?mc_cid=f1652b9096&mc_eid=cd93417b7c |website=Charlotte Lozier Institute |access-date=4 August 2021}}</ref> to the United States Supreme Court in the case of ''[[Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization|Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health]]'' which overturned the Court's previous ruling in ''[[Roe v. Wade]]''.

Therein Condic summarizes her perspective on biomedical advances published in scientific journals that have increased biological understanding of human fetal development. However, many of her cited sources are misrepresented. For instance, citing a 2015 study by Lutkenhoff and colleagues,<ref name="Lutkenhoff 68–76">{{Cite journal |last1=Lutkenhoff |first1=Evan S. |last2=Chiang |first2=Jeffrey |last3=Tshibanda |first3=Luaba |last4=Kamau |first4=Evelyn |last5=Kirsch |first5=Murielle |last6=Pickard |first6=John D. |last7=Laureys |first7=Steven |last8=Owen |first8=Adrian M. |last9=Monti |first9=Martin M. |date=July 2015 |title=Thalamic and extrathalamic mechanisms of consciousness after severe brain injury: Brain Injury and Consciousness |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ana.24423 |journal=Annals of Neurology |language=en |volume=78 |issue=1 |pages=68–76 |doi=10.1002/ana.24423|pmid=25893530 |hdl=2268/183269 |s2cid=10774807 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> Condic writes that "the largest study to date of human patients with consciousness disorders unambiguously concluded that the loss of consciousness is associated not with the loss of cortical, but rather of subcortical circuitry." This would appear to suggest that consciousness might arise early in gestation even before the [[cerebral cortex]] has developed if, for instance, anatomical brain structures situated below the cortex, such as the [[thalamus]], are actually responsible for [[consciousness]]. However, this interpretation is contradicted by the very study it cites, in which Lutkenhoff and colleagues<ref name="Lutkenhoff 68–76"/> endorse the view of an earlier study<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Fuller |first1=Patrick |last2=Sherman |first2=David |last3=Pedersen |first3=Nigel P. |last4=Saper |first4=Clifford B. |last5=Lu |first5=Jun |date=2011-04-01 |title=Reassessment of the structural basis of the ascending arousal system |journal=The Journal of Comparative Neurology |language=en |volume=519 |issue=5 |pages=933–956 |doi=10.1002/cne.22559 |pmc=3119596 |pmid=21280045}}</ref> that the thalamus "might itself be neither necessary nor sufficient to produce wakefulness." The cerebral cortex appears to rely on nerve fibers that project from the thalamus, thus consciousness may be lost when the thalamus is injured, yet this does not demonstrate that consciousness can be sustained by the thalamus alone.<ref name="Lutkenhoff 68–76"/> Furthermore, the fact that the cortex relies on the thalamus to function is evidence that consciousness cannot plausibly emerge prior to 24 weeks gestation when connections form between the thalamus and cortex.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Padilla |first1=Nelly |last2=Lagercrantz |first2=Hugo |date=May 2020 |title=Making of the mind |journal=Acta Paediatrica |language=en |volume=109 |issue=5 |pages=883–892 |doi=10.1111/apa.15167 |pmid=31922622 |s2cid=210133737 |issn=0803-5253|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Condic states in her amicus that "...technological breakthroughs, especially sophisticated brain mapping and 4D ultrasonography, have enabled direct, unprecedented observation of human fetuses and behavior indicating their subjective experiences— confirming that the fetus is living, conscious, and sensitive to pain shortly after the beginning of the second trimester and months before viability."<ref>{{Cite web| title=Brief of maureen l. condic, ph.d. and the charlotte lozier institute as amici curiae supporting petitioners | url=https://www.supremecourt.gov/DocketPDF/19/19-1392/185364/20210729171818898_CondicCLI%20Amicus%20Brief%20Final.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210730124607/https://www.supremecourt.gov/DocketPDF/19/19-1392/185364/20210729171818898_CondicCLI%20Amicus%20Brief%20Final.pdf | archive-date=2021-07-30}}</ref> She argues that many of the scientific "uncertainties" that were present when ''Roe'' was decided five decades ago have subsequently been clarified by scientific advances. However, these advances in neuroscience do not corroborate her view that fetuses are conscious prior to viability. For instance, a 2021 study of fetal [[Magnetoencephalography|MEG]] signals found that a signature of conscious processing was not present until 35 weeks gestation, i.e., during the third trimester when the fetus is already viable.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Moser |first1=Julia |last2=Schleger |first2=Franziska |last3=Weiss |first3=Magdalene |last4=Sippel |first4=Katrin |last5=Semeia |first5=Lorenzo |last6=Preissl |first6=Hubert |date=2021-06-01 |title=Magnetoencephalographic signatures of conscious processing before birth |journal=Developmental Cognitive Neuroscience |language=en |volume=49 |article-number=100964 |doi=10.1016/j.dcn.2021.100964 |pmid=34023644 |pmc=8163957 |s2cid=235167579 |issn=1878-9293}}</ref>
